title: there's no point in -ing, it's worth -ing etc.
subtitle: no point in -ing / worth -ing / trouble -ing / go -ing
summary: Use the -ing form after there's no point in, it's no use, it's worth, have trouble, spend time, be busy and go (for sports and activities).

lesson.heading: there's no point in / it's no use / it's no good
lesson.text: To say that doing something is useless, we say **there's no point in doing**, **it's no use doing** or **it's no good doing** something. Note that we say *no point in* but *the point of*.

examples.text: **There's no point in having** a car if you never use it.
**There was no point in waiting** any longer, so we left.
**It's no use worrying** about what happened. There's nothing you can do about it.
**It's no good trying** to persuade me. You won't succeed.
What's **the point of having** a car if you never use it?
examples.note: the point of ... but no point in ...

lesson.heading: it's worth / it's not worth
lesson.text: We say **it's worth doing** or **it's not worth doing** something. You can also say that something **is worth it** or **not worth it**, and that a place is *worth visiting*, a movie is *worth seeing* etc.

examples.text: It's a nice town. **It's worth spending** a few days there.
Our flight was very early in the morning, so **it wasn't worth going** to bed.
You should spend a couple of days here. **It's worth it.**
It's a great movie. **It's worth seeing.**
Thieves broke into the house, but didn't take anything. There was **nothing worth stealing**.
It's an interesting idea. **It's worth thinking about.**

lesson.heading: have trouble / difficulty / a problem doing something
lesson.text: After **have trouble**, **have difficulty** and **have a problem** we use **-ing**, not *to ...*.

examples.text: I **had no trouble finding** a place to stay.
Did you **have a problem getting** a visa?
People sometimes **have difficulty reading** my writing.

lesson.heading: spend / waste time doing; be busy doing
lesson.text: We say **spend (time) doing** and **waste (time) doing** something. We also say **(be) busy doing** something.

examples.text: He **spent hours trying** to repair the clock.
I **waste a lot of time doing** nothing.
She said she couldn't meet me. She was too **busy doing** other things.

lesson.heading: go swimming / go skiing etc.
lesson.text: We use **go -ing** for sports and other activities: *go sailing, go swimming, go fishing, go riding, go hiking, go surfing, go scuba diving, go skiing, go jogging, go camping*.

examples.text: How often do you **go swimming**?
We **went skiing** last year.
Tom isn't here. He's **gone shopping**.
I've never **been sailing**.

lesson.heading: Summary: expressions followed by -ing
rows: it's no use / it's no good

lesson.text: *Worth* is always followed by -ing, never by *to*: *It's worth seeing* (not ~~worth to see~~).

exercises.prompt: It's a great movie. It's worth ___.
Which sentence follows which? Match the pairs.

pairs.right: It's worth spending a few days here.

pairs.left: It's no use standing here talking.
There's no point in looking for him.
It's no good apologising to me.
It's not worth arguing with him.

exercises.prompt: I waste too much time ___ TV.
exercises.explanation: waste time + -ing: I waste too much time watching TV.

exercises.prompt: Karen is going on holiday tomorrow, so she's busy ___ her things ready.
exercises.explanation: be busy + -ing: she's busy getting her things ready.

exercises.prompt: Why work if you don't need money? Say this with There's no point ... .
exercises.answer: There's no point in working if you don't need money.

exercises.prompt: I find it hard to remember people's names. I have a problem ___.
exercises.explanation: have a problem + -ing: I have a problem remembering people's names.

exercises.statement: I had no trouble to find a place to stay.
exercises.explanation: I had no trouble finding a place to stay. After have trouble we use -ing, not to + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: It was a very hot day, so we ___ in the lake.
exercises.explanation: go + -ing for activities, in the past simple: we went swimming.

exercises.prompt: Dan isn't here. He ___. There were a few things he needed to buy.
exercises.explanation: go + -ing: He's gone shopping (he is still out) or He went shopping.

exercises.prompt: What's ___ having a car if you never use it?
exercises.explanation: We say there's no point in ..., but What's the point of ...?

exercises.prompt: It was easy for us to understand one another. We had no difficulty ___.
exercises.explanation: have difficulty + -ing: We had no difficulty understanding one another.

exercises.prompt: Why hurry if you have plenty of time? Say this with There's no point ... .
exercises.answer: There's no point in hurrying if you have plenty of time.
